Read that test file first; it is the spec and you must not edit it. Fixed window per key, deny does not extend the window, retryAfterSec is whole seconds rounded up (min 1), fail closed for new keys when maxKeys live keys are tracked (evict expired keys first). No dependencies.

T-p2-ratelimit.summary: Added apps/api/src/ratelimit.ts with createRateLimiter({limit, windowMs, maxKeys?, now?}) returning {check, sweep, size}. It uses a fixed window per key, and a denied request does not extend the window. retryAfterSec is whole seconds rounded up, minimum 1. A new key is refused when maxKeys live keys are tracked, after expired keys are evicted first. It throws on invalid config: limit must be a positive integer, windowMs positive, and maxKeys a positive integer. maxKeys defaults to 10000 and now defaults to Date.now. There are no dependencies. The test file was not edited.

testsExecuted.result: passed: exited 0. It printed a baseUrl warning about tsconfig.json lines 21-24; the file is unchanged and I did not look into the warning.

criteriaSatisfied: Fixed window per key; deny does not extend the window
retryAfterSec is whole seconds rounded up, minimum 1
New keys fail closed when maxKeys live keys are tracked, after evicting expired keys
Only apps/api/src/ratelimit.ts was written; no dependencies
risks: Allowed results report retryAfterSec: 0 (the spec only constrains it for denies).
A fail-closed denial for a new key reports a retryAfterSec of a full window, which can overstate the wait. It could be tightened to the earliest live key expiry.
The module is not yet wired into any route; no other apps/api file was touched.
maxKeys default of 10000 is my choice; the spec gave none.
